provenance.what: The language-neutral oracle for node-graph WIRE editing and minimap navigation: an authored port graph + a pointer gesture named in port terms -> the wire edits the host journals for the guest, and the camera a minimap click moves to.
provenance.why: `DagHost` has had port/handle hit-testing and an `InteractionMode::DrawEdge` since it was written, but only its `pointer_*_screen` entry reaches them. The wgpu renderer called ONLY the bounded `plan_pointer`/`commit_pointer` entry, whose gesture vocabulary is Idle|Pan|Drag|Select and whose `bounded_node_hit_index` answers `Unsupported` for exactly the port, handle, widget and minimap hits — so a press on a port aborted the dispatch instead of starting a wire, and a minimap click navigated nowhere. Port-to-port wire creation, wire removal and minimap click-to-navigate were dead from wgpu's side. Ticket 26/09/09/PROCEDURAL-3D-END-TO-END, 📓️audit-wgpu-parity-2026-09-13.md gaps #2 and #5.
provenance.rule: A completed gesture journals what it did to the GRAPH in the guest's own vocabulary — never in engine handle or edge ids, and never as a whole re-serialised fixture.
provenance.reference: React dispatches the same vocabulary from ReactFlow's own `onConnect` (🕸️NodeGraph/🟦️.tsx), and the guest decodes it as `FlowNodeGraphEditOp` (✏️s/🔌️plugins/🌊️flow/…/🎮️commands/✏️node-graph-edit/🦀️.rs).

rules.portGrammar: A wire endpoint is named '<nodeId>@<portId>' — the same pick/hover channel grammar the graph already reports hover targets in, so a journalled edit is a lookup on what the host already knows, not a second derivation.
rules.connectIsFourIds: A created wire dispatches ONE narrow operation carrying four ids: {operation: 'connect', sourceNodeId, sourcePortId, targetNodeId, targetPortId}. Re-publishing the whole fixture instead (React's own `commitFixture`) cannot fit a bounded action and is not required — the guest already declares this operation.
rules.targetPortHoldsOne: An input port holds at most one incoming wire: connecting a second one removes the first, and BOTH halves are journalled — the removal as {operation: 'disconnect', edgeId} naming the synapse id the guest knows, the creation as its own connect.
rules.unknownEdgeIsSilent: A removed edge the guest never learned about (one this very gesture created) carries no synapse id and is not journalled — there is nothing for the guest to remove.
rules.drainedOnce: The journal is drained by the renderer after each gesture; a second drain of the same gesture yields nothing, so one wire is never dispatched twice.
rules.minimapClickNavigates: A press inside the minimap panel but outside its viewport rectangle re-centres the camera on the world point under the pointer. A press inside the viewport rectangle instead begins a drag of that rectangle, leaving the camera where it was until the pointer moves.
rules.screenPathOwnsTheGesture: While any of these interactions is in flight the bounded plan path must not claim the follow-up move/up — the host answers `screenPointerGestureActive` for exactly that window.

graph.why: Two computation nodes far enough apart that no proximity connection fires on its own, so every wire in this oracle is one the gesture actually drew.

cases.name: drag-output-port-to-input-port-creates-a-wire
cases.why: The whole gap, stated once: this gesture is what a user does to wire two operators together, and on wgpu it did nothing at all.

cases.name: a-second-wire-into-the-same-input-replaces-the-first
cases.why: An input port holds one wire — the replaced one must reach the guest as a disconnect, or the guest's graph keeps an edge the user can no longer see.

cases.name: the-journal-drains-once
cases.why: The renderer drains after every gesture; a wire dispatched twice would ask the guest to connect what it already connected.

cases.name: a-press-on-a-port-belongs-to-the-screen-path
cases.why: The discriminator itself: the bounded plan path must hand this gesture over instead of faulting on it.

cases.name: a-press-on-empty-canvas-stays-on-the-bounded-path
cases.why: The other half — marquee selection and node dragging must keep their atomically-admitted plan/commit path.

minimap.why: `minimap_widget_pointer_hit` is reached only from `pointer_down_screen`/`pointer_move_screen`, so it inherited the wire gap rather than being a separate one.
